jsonld.name: Chicken Pastilla
jsonld.description: The pastilla is the Moroccan canon's crown: a round of near-transparent warqa leaves — "paper," the thinnest pastry on earth — wrapped in many layers around a filling of chicken slow-cooked with onions until the two become one, bound with beaten eggs and seasoned with saffron and ginger, and crowned with a second stratum: almonds fried in oil, crushed with cinnamon and sugar. Savory and sweet in alternating layers, the whole baked to a shattering gold and served whole, the first slice's cross-section the table's theater. It is Fès's dish, the great occasions' dish, and the most complete single-plate argument this cuisine makes.
recipeIngredient: 1 pack frozen warqa (about 20 leaves — Middle Eastern groceries; see the note) or 12 sheets phyllo, each brushed generously with melted butter (the bridge — heavier, still true) — or the from-scratch warqa: 500 g flour, ½ tsp salt, and 700 ml water whisked to a thin batter, rested 1 hour, and dabbed by a honey-daubed pad onto a convex pan or an upturned crepe pan at its medium heat, the leaves lifted as they set — a craft of its own, and the #38's cousins' law
1.5 kg chicken (a whole fowl, or bone-in thighs), cut to pieces
4 large onions (about 800 g), sliced paper-thin (the food processor's finest blade is honest here — the onions must melt)
1½ tsp saffron (about 1 g), steeped in 4 tbsp hot water (#120); 2 tbsp ground ginger; 1 tsp white pepper; ½ tsp cinnamon; 1½ tsp salt
3 tbsp butter (about 45 g); a fist of cilantro and parsley (about 30 g), tied; 200 ml water (about 200 g)
The juice of ½ a lemon (about 20 ml); 1 tsp cinnamon; a pinch of sugar (about 2 g)
300 g whole almonds, skins off (blanched 2 minutes, pinched), fried in 3 tbsp neutral oil (about 40 g) to deep gold
3 tbsp powdered sugar (about 25 g); 1½ tbsp ground cinnamon (about 8 g) — half mixed into the crushed almonds, half held for the dusting
Butter (about 60 g), melted, for the leaves; 1 egg yolk (about 20 g) for the seal's shine

recipeInstructions.name: Step 1
recipeInstructions.text: The slow pot. Melt the butter in a wide, heavy pot; add the chicken pieces, the sliced onions, the saffron water, the spices, the herbs, and the salt; stir over medium 5 minutes to the pot's perfume. Add the water, cover, and adjust to the barest tremble (roughly 95 °C) for 1 hour — until the chicken is falling-tender and the onions have melted entirely to a golden, saffron-scented silk. Checkpoint: the pot's end: the chicken lifted to a bowl (the meat stripped from the bones and the skin, and the bones discarded — the filling is boneless by law), and the onions' silk left in the pot's bottom — no separate liquid should remain; if some does, simmer it uncovered until the silk alone holds the spoon.

recipeInstructions.name: Step 2
recipeInstructions.text: The eggs' binding. Return the stripped chicken to the onion silk over low heat, pour in the beaten eggs, and stir constantly 3 to 4 minutes — the eggs set in soft curds through the silk, binding the whole to a moist, spoonable mass. The lemon, cinnamon, and the pinch of sugar at the end; taste — the savory layer should be deeply seasoned, the ginger and saffron forward, faintly sweet beneath. Checkpoint: the filling's texture: moist but holding — a spoonful mounds and keeps its shape. Wet filling soaks the warqa; over-dry filling loses the dish. The eggs' soft curds are the binder — scrambled to silk, not to rubber, at the low heat's patience.

recipeInstructions.name: Step 3
recipeInstructions.text: Fry, crush, perfume. Fry the blanched almonds in the oil over medium until deep gold — 6 to 8 minutes, shaking, watched at the end (the line between gold and burnt is a minute) — and drain. Crush them coarsely (the rolling pin between parchment, or a few pulses — texture, not powder) and mix with half the cinnamon-sugar. Checkpoint: the almonds should be fragrant, oily-gold, and crushed to rubble — the crown's texture is the bite against the warqa's shatter. The cinnamon-sugar's mix should perfume without sweetness-dominance; the dusting half is held back.

recipeInstructions.name: Step 4
recipeInstructions.text: The wrap, in the round. Butter a 25 cm round pan or oven dish lavishly. Lay the first warqa leaf (or two, overlapping) to overhang the pan's rim by 5 cm all around; brush with butter. Build: 3 more leaves, each brushed, layered slightly rotated. Then the first stratum — half the chicken-egg filling, spread to the edge — and 2 more buttered leaves over. The almond stratum: the crushed cinnamon almonds spread even. Two more leaves. The remaining chicken filling. Then the wrap's close: the overhanging leaves folded in over the top, and 2 to 3 fresh leaves laid over all, tucked down the pan's sides, buttered, and the whole pressed gently compact. The egg yolk brushed over the top's face. Checkpoint: the wrapped pastilla should sit firm and level — a drum's top, not a dome — its walls of many leaves, its layers' order the dish's architecture: savory, sweet, savory, with the pastry's butter between every stratum. The butter is the glue and the shatter's promise; brush with generosity.

recipeInstructions.name: Step 5
recipeInstructions.text: The bake (35 minutes at 180 °C). Bake at 180 °C until the top and the walls carry a deep, blistered gold — 30 to 35 minutes, turning once at the 20th — and the butter's perfume has filled the kitchen. Rest 10 minutes. Checkpoint: the gold's depth is the shatter's promise: pale pastilla is soft pastilla. The rest's ten minutes sets the layers for the slice.

recipeInstructions.name: Step 6
recipeInstructions.text: The crown and the first slice. Dust the whole with the held-back cinnamon-sugar in the traditional's fine lattice (a stencil, or the fingers' pinch-lines through a sieve), and carry it to the table whole. The first slice is cut at the table — the cross-section's strata, warqa and filling alternating, the theater the dish has earned. Checkpoint: eating test: the warqa's shatter — crackling, buttery, gone in a breath — then the savory stratum's silk: saffron-ginger chicken bound in egg and onion-melt, deeply savory and faintly sweet; then the almond layer's cinnamon-sugar crunch between the two savories' silk; and the pastry again. Each bite should assemble the pastilla's whole argument: paper and filling, savory and sweet, silk and shatter — and the table's argument, served.

Chicken Pastilla

Moroccan · Hard · Makes one 25 cm pastilla (serves 6–8)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The pastilla is the Moroccan canon's crown: a round of near-transparent warqa leaves — "paper," the thinnest pastry on earth — wrapped in many layers around a filling of chicken slow-cooked with onions until the two become one, bound with beaten eggs and seasoned with saffron and ginger, and crowned with a second stratum: almonds fried in oil, crushed with cinnamon and sugar. Savory and sweet in alternating layers, the whole baked to a shattering gold and served whole, the first slice's cross-section the table's theater. It is Fès's dish, the great occasions' dish, and the most complete single-plate argument this cuisine makes.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The warqa (or the honest bridge)

The chicken and its onion sauce

  • the onions must melt)

The egg binding

The almond crown

  • half mixed into the crushed almonds, half held for the dusting

The bridges, honestly stated:

frozen warqa is the working truth (thawed, kept under a damp towel like the brik's malsouka, #1's own law); phyllo bridges at a heavier crunch — brush every leaf generously with butter and accept the difference. The almonds want the frying (their oil-toasts are the crown's depth); the oven-toasted bridge is acceptable and lighter. What cannot bridge: the two-layer filling's architecture — the savory's eggs and the sweet's almonds are the dish's identity, and a pastilla of one register is a different, lesser thing.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • The pot: onions melted to silk, the chicken stripped and returned, the eggs bound soft.
  • The crown: gold-fried almonds, crushed to rubble, half-perfumed.
  • The wrap: many leaves, butter between, drum-flat, baked to blistered gold.
  • The table: dusted in lattice, sliced at the table, the strata shown.

Chicken Pastilla

Prep: 1 hour 30 minutes · Cook: 1 hour 30 minutes · Total: About 3 hours (plus the warqa's prep or thaw) · Makes one 25 cm pastilla (serves 6–8)

Ingredients

The warqa (or the honest bridge)

  • 1 pack frozen warqa (about 20 leaves — Middle Eastern groceries; see the note) or 12 sheets phyllo, each brushed generously with melted butter (the bridge — heavier, still true) — or the from-scratch warqa: 500 g flour, ½ tsp salt, and 700 ml water whisked to a thin batter, rested 1 hour, and dabbed by a honey-daubed pad onto a convex pan or an upturned crepe pan at its medium heat, the leaves lifted as they set — a craft of its own, and the #38's cousins' law

The chicken and its onion sauce

  • 1.5 kg chicken (a whole fowl, or bone-in thighs), cut to pieces
  • 4 large onions (about 800 g), sliced paper-thin (the food processor's finest blade is honest here — the onions must melt)
  • 1½ tsp saffron (about 1 g), steeped in 4 tbsp hot water (#120); 2 tbsp ground ginger; 1 tsp white pepper; ½ tsp cinnamon; 1½ tsp salt
  • 3 tbsp butter (about 45 g); a fist of cilantro and parsley (about 30 g), tied; 200 ml water (about 200 g)

The egg binding

  • 6 eggs (about 300 g), beaten
  • The juice of ½ a lemon (about 20 ml); 1 tsp cinnamon; a pinch of sugar (about 2 g)

The almond crown

  • 300 g whole almonds, skins off (blanched 2 minutes, pinched), fried in 3 tbsp neutral oil (about 40 g) to deep gold
  • 3 tbsp powdered sugar (about 25 g); 1½ tbsp ground cinnamon (about 8 g) — half mixed into the crushed almonds, half held for the dusting
  • Butter (about 60 g), melted, for the leaves; 1 egg yolk (about 20 g) for the seal's shine

The bridges, honestly stated:

    Instructions

    1. **The slow pot.** Melt the butter in a wide, heavy pot; add the chicken pieces, the sliced onions, the saffron water, the spices, the herbs, and the salt; stir over medium 5 minutes to the pot's perfume. Add the water, cover, and adjust to the barest tremble (roughly 95 °C) for 1 hour — until the chicken is falling-tender and the onions have melted entirely to a golden, saffron-scented silk. Checkpoint — the pot's end: the chicken lifted to a bowl (the meat stripped from the bones and the skin, and the bones discarded — the filling is boneless by law), and the onions' silk left in the pot's bottom — no separate liquid should remain; if some does, simmer it uncovered until the silk alone holds the spoon.
    2. **The eggs' binding.** Return the stripped chicken to the onion silk over low heat, pour in the beaten eggs, and stir constantly 3 to 4 minutes — the eggs set in soft curds through the silk, binding the whole to a moist, spoonable mass. The lemon, cinnamon, and the pinch of sugar at the end; taste — the savory layer should be deeply seasoned, the ginger and saffron forward, faintly sweet beneath. Checkpoint — the filling's texture: moist but holding — a spoonful mounds and keeps its shape. Wet filling soaks the warqa; over-dry filling loses the dish. The eggs' soft curds are the binder — scrambled to silk, not to rubber, at the low heat's patience.
    3. **Fry, crush, perfume.** Fry the blanched almonds in the oil over medium until deep gold — 6 to 8 minutes, shaking, watched at the end (the line between gold and burnt is a minute) — and drain. Crush them coarsely (the rolling pin between parchment, or a few pulses — texture, not powder) and mix with half the cinnamon-sugar. Checkpoint — the almonds should be fragrant, oily-gold, and crushed to rubble — the crown's texture is the bite against the warqa's shatter. The cinnamon-sugar's mix should perfume without sweetness-dominance; the dusting half is held back.
    4. **The wrap, in the round.** Butter a 25 cm round pan or oven dish lavishly. Lay the first warqa leaf (or two, overlapping) to overhang the pan's rim by 5 cm all around; brush with butter. Build: 3 more leaves, each brushed, layered slightly rotated. Then the first stratum — half the chicken-egg filling, spread to the edge — and 2 more buttered leaves over. The almond stratum: the crushed cinnamon almonds spread even. Two more leaves. The remaining chicken filling. Then the wrap's close: the overhanging leaves folded in over the top, and 2 to 3 fresh leaves laid over all, tucked down the pan's sides, buttered, and the whole pressed gently compact. The egg yolk brushed over the top's face. Checkpoint — the wrapped pastilla should sit firm and level — a drum's top, not a dome — its walls of many leaves, its layers' order the dish's architecture: savory, sweet, savory, with the pastry's butter between every stratum. The butter is the glue and the shatter's promise; brush with generosity.
    5. **The bake (35 minutes at 180 °C).** Bake at 180 °C until the top and the walls carry a deep, blistered gold — 30 to 35 minutes, turning once at the 20th — and the butter's perfume has filled the kitchen. Rest 10 minutes. Checkpoint — the gold's depth is the shatter's promise: pale pastilla is soft pastilla. The rest's ten minutes sets the layers for the slice.
    6. **The crown and the first slice.** Dust the whole with the held-back cinnamon-sugar in the traditional's fine lattice (a stencil, or the fingers' pinch-lines through a sieve), and carry it to the table whole. The first slice is cut at the table — the cross-section's strata, warqa and filling alternating, the theater the dish has earned. Checkpoint — eating test: the warqa's shatter — crackling, buttery, gone in a breath — then the savory stratum's silk: saffron-ginger chicken bound in egg and onion-melt, deeply savory and faintly sweet; then the almond layer's cinnamon-sugar crunch between the two savories' silk; and the pastry again. Each bite should assemble the pastilla's whole argument: paper and filling, savory and sweet, silk and shatter — and the table's argument, served.

    Finish & Plate

    Whole to the table on the round — the lattice's dust, the gold's blister — and sliced before the diners: six or eight wedges, each plated with its cross-section up, the pastilla's argument served in its own presentation.

    Troubleshooting

    SymptomCauseFix
    Filling soaked the pastryWet chicken-egg filling or butter-sparse leavesReduce the silk; brush every leaf
    Pastilla fell at the sliceUnder-bound eggs or an under-baked wallThe soft curds' full set; the deep-gold bake
    One-note savoryThe almond stratum thin or its sugar shyThe crown is half the dish \u2014 build it

    Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

    - The baked pastilla keeps 1 day (re-crisps 10 minutes at 180 °C — a fair second slice); the assembled unbaked keeps 1 day refrigerated, 2 weeks frozen. The fillings keep 2 days separately. - Variations: the Fès pigeon original, the coast's seafood version, the milk-soaked sweet pastilla of the wedding canon. This record is the site's A-tier master; the #34 couscous and the #31 m'qualli are its canon-mates at the grand table.
